title: Getting started: a guide for beginners
subtitle: Choose a starting point that suits you. No coding experience needed for the chatbot or desktop routes.
intro: You do not need to learn every term or use a terminal before trying AI. Choose one of the three routes below, then check what you learned. There is no timer or required sequence; account setup and project work may need a separate session.
boundary: ONLY public information; nothing OFFICIAL or non-public. NEVER connect to government networks or accounts. Use the designated non-government learning network. If you are unsure about the device, network or learning account, ask the facilitator before proceeding.

steps.title: Check what information you can use
steps.body: Use the supplied fictional examples or independently public material. Do not bring an internal work document, even with names removed. Check which learning network and accounts you may use. If there is no facilitator, ask the person responsible for the device; stay with the offline activities until setup is confirmed.

paths.title: Try a chatbot
paths.subtitle: For a first conversation with AI. No terminal or project setup.
paths.body: Use a fictional community-garden invitation to practise giving instructions and checking an answer. The exercise includes a prompt, source facts and an example you can review offline.
steps: Open the chatbot exercise and read the supplied facts.
If a permitted learning account is ready, choose a chatbot from Web & media. Check account settings and costs before pasting the exercise prompt; do not connect other accounts or files.
Compare the reply with the supplied facts. Ask for one correction and check whether it fixed the problem.
paths.check: You can point to a supported fact, an unsupported addition and a useful follow-up request.

paths.title: Get comfortable with this desktop
paths.subtitle: For anyone new to Omarchy or terminals. Works offline.
paths.body: Learn how to find an app, switch windows, make a window fullscreen and close it after saving. The terminal practice is a simulation: it does not run commands or read your files.
steps: Open Omarchy help and find fullscreen, close-window and window-switching controls. Save work before trying window controls.
Read Your first commands, explained below, then open the terminal simulation. Each step separates what to type, what it means and what you should see.
Follow the seven practice steps one at a time. Compare the displayed folder before and after changing location, then read the project instructions again.
paths.check: You can find the window controls and explain why changing folders changes which files a command can find.

paths.title: Build your first project
paths.subtitle: For learners ready to use a coding agent. Tool setup required.
paths.body: A coding agent can change files and run tools. Ask which agent is prepared for this device, how to sign in and what spending limits apply. A detected command alone does not confirm readiness. Do not install software just to finish this route.
steps: Open Your first agent session and create a project. Read BRIEF.md, the text file describing what to make.
Choose the prepared agent in the project and paste the starter prompt inside the assistant, not at the shell prompt. Review actions before approving them.
Compare the resulting page with the brief. Try its controls and a narrow window, then ask for a specific correction if needed.
paths.check: You can find your project, demonstrate one check and explain a limitation of the result.

offline.title: No account or internet? You can still practise
offline.body: Use the desktop route, read AI basics or review the chatbot exercise’s authored sample. These are offline learning activities, not AI-generated work. You can also create the first-project starter and inspect its brief without opening an agent. Do not try to bypass missing accounts or network restrictions.

check: Explain one thing you checked rather than only whether you liked the output. When finished, save any work and use the Finish session checklist.

title: Finish session
subtitle: Save your work, review accounts and prepare for handover.
intro: Use this manual checklist before leaving the laptop. It is not an automatic logout or device reset. Tick steps you have reviewed, including those not applicable. Ticks reset on reload and are not saved or scored.
boundary: Continue to use ONLY public information; nothing OFFICIAL. NEVER connect to government networks or accounts to save, email or transfer your practice work. Follow the facilitator’s approved handover procedure.

steps.title: Save and locate your work
steps.body: Save changes in the editor or tool and confirm you can find the project in My projects. Do not assume an assistant’s final message means every file was saved. Agree how public practice work is retained before an account reset; this checklist does not delete or export anything.

steps.title: Stop tasks and close tools
steps.body: Use each tool’s own controls to stop active requests or jobs, then close the intended windows after saving. Check for background tasks with the facilitator if unsure. Closing the Labs window does not stop its hub, other tools or provider-side jobs.

steps.title: Review keys held by Labs
steps.body: Use Forget keys held by Labs below. This prevents Labs supplying those keys to future launches; it does not remove credentials already held or saved by tools, revoke provider keys, or sign out accounts. Review this step even if you did not enter a key here.

steps.title: Sign out of external accounts
steps.body: Sign out of any learning websites and native tools you used, following the local shared-device procedure. Check the actual service or tool rather than assuming a closed window ended the login. Labs cannot inspect or verify those sign-outs, browser cookies or tool credential stores.

steps.title: Check the handover procedure
steps.body: Follow the agreed account/device handover process with the facilitator or device owner. Projects and bookmarks belong to the Linux account and may be visible to its next user. If the procedure is unclear, do not pass an active learning account to someone else.

incident: If you suspect non-public information or a key was exposed, stop the task and contact the facilitator/deployment owner using the agreed incident process. Do not paste the material into another AI tool or a support form. If connected to a government network, disconnect the learning device and report it. Exposed keys may need provider revocation; forgetting them here is not revocation.
